paper_claims.claim: The original MAX measure (average of 5 highest daily returns in a month) reliably negatively predicts one-month-ahead value-weighted stock returns; the alpha is robust to standard risk factors (FF3, FF5, FF6).

The new MAX^\beta measure (a non-parametric beta-neutralization of MAX via a 10x10 double sort on market beta then MAX) produces a robust, two-sided long-short anomaly whose alpha is large and statistically significant under standard risk factors (FF3, FF5, FF6).

MAX-sorted portfolios correlate monotonically with market beta and idiosyncratic volatility, implying the original MAX anomaly is confounded by systematic risk rather than a pure preference-based proxy.
MAX^\beta construction successfully neutralizes market beta across deciles and the IVOL/BETA spreads between extreme MAX^\beta deciles shrink relative to the univariate MAX sort.

tables.description: Univariate decile sorts on MAX: VW excess returns and 9-factor alphas (we replicate the 6 in-FF columns; SY/DHS/FFCPS/FF6PS dropped per Assumptions 1-3).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of MAX (average of the 5 highest daily returns), correct value-weighting of the excess-return portfolios, correct Newey-West (1987) standard errors with 6 lags, and correct alignment of the FF factor library. Downstream claim C1 depends on this table.
tables.paper_quote: Consistent with the findings of Bali et al. (2011), we document a significantly negative cross-sectional relationship between MAX and next-month returns ... a value-weighted average return spread of -0.95% per month, which is statistically significant with a Newey-West (1987) t-statistic of -3.08.
tables.notes: Dropped SY/DHS/FFCPS/FF6PS from per-cell target list since the third-party factors are unavailable in ClickHouse.

tables.description: MAX^\beta-sorted decile portfolios: VW excess returns and 9-factor alphas — the central finding. SY/DHS/FFCPS/FF6PS dropped per Assumptions 1-3.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of MAX^\beta via the two-stage beta-then-MAX sort. Downstream claim C2 depends on this table.
tables.paper_quote: The average return spread between the high- and low-MAX^\beta portfolios is -0.81% per month and highly significant with a t-statistic of -3.62.

tables.description: Cross-sectional medians of MAX, BETA, IVOL across MAX-sorted decile portfolios — diagnostic of construction.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates (a) MAX is monotonically increasing across the deciles (sanity check that the sort works), (b) BETA rises monotonically with MAX (showing systematic risk confounding), (c) IVOL rises monotonically with MAX. Downstream claim C3 depends on these patterns.
tables.paper_quote: MAX increases monotonically from 1% to 7.1% per day. More importantly, we find a strong positive correlation between MAX and several indicators of risk and overvaluation. Market beta (BETA) rises significantly from 0.581 to 1.043 across the deciles ... high-MAX stocks are significantly smaller and exhibit higher idiosyncratic volatility (IVOL).
